validator_result: OK. There are no errors and no ATYPICAL lines for either unit. The only warnings are the expected ones: the patterns repair-allies and lay-mines are planned but not written yet, and the unit links ra1.shared.ore-truck and ra1.soviet.yak point to units nobody has researched yet.
copy_check_result: Exit 0. All 10 cited pages were checked and no runs of six or more words are shared. The two manual scans are cited as File: pages, and for those pages the wiki API returns only a licence template. So the manual wording was checked in two other ways: through the wiki quote boxes that copy the manual paragraphs (Field mechanic, Anti-tank minelayer, Anti-personnel minelayer), and by my own local six-word check against the text pulled from both PDFs. That local check also covered the uncited pages: Yak, the manual transcript, StrategyWiki's Soviet units page, and BDATA.CPP, UDATA.CPP, IDATA.CPP, RULES.CPP and FOOT.CPP. It found nothing.

hesitations.reason: The task fixed the id, and the evidence supports one shared entry. UNIT.CPP has a single MNLY type that lays an anti-personnel mine for the USSR, Ukraine and the Soviet side and an anti-tank mine for everyone else. Both infoboxes give the same internal name, price, speed, sight and health. Against that: the manual prints two paragraphs, the wiki has two pages, registry choice 6 does not list the minelayer among RA1's shared units, and the research notes speak of 'both minelayers'. The Ids convention ('shared' is for units every side can field) does not say what to do when one shared type behaves differently per side.

roles.primary says to use only what every copy has, and the registry says a shared unit's official text counts only where every side's version carries it. The Allied copies' mines would support anti-armour, but anti-armour's requires need a damage type, which an ability cannot carry. The Soviet copies' mines would support anti-infantry, but only half the copies have them. The roles.secondary steps do not say how to rank a button whose effect differs by side. Recorded in fit_notes.

Laying a mine is a one-off action on the deploy key, not a stationary mode, so the toggle-or-deploy tie-break does not apply.

source_problems:
1. The manual scans can't be checked automatically. Through the wiki API, the File: pages for both manual scans return only a licence template, so the copy-check cannot compare paraphrases with the manuals. I read the PDFs themselves from static.wikia.nocookie.net instead.

2. The game's rules.ini was not readable (the registry notes say the same). That leaves several facts unconfirmed:
- the wrench's reach, rate and delivery;
- the minelayer's Tracked flag;
- the Crewed flag, which decides on_death;
- the mine damage per armour type.

3. Problems with the Field Mechanic page:
- The infobox armortype (Light) conflicts with the manual's armour grade (None).
- Its 'cooldown 25' cites IDATA.CPP line 1025. That line is the frame on which the projectile launches, not a cooldown.
- The manual calls him slow, but the infobox speed equals the Rifle Infantry's.

4. Problems with the minelayer pages:
- The Anti-tank minelayer infobox has no armortype.
- The Anti-personnel page says Soviet troops avoid their own mines, but the code applies that avoidance to both sides through a rules setting.

5. Visibility of mines: no page read says whether enemy players can see laid mines. BDATA.CPP marks the mines as invisible to radar, unselectable and not a legal target.

6. Uncertain version of the APC rule: the force-move exception that lets the mechanic board a damaged APC is in the 2020 source release. Whether the 1997-1999 game had it is unchecked.

All pages loaded; there were no 429s or fetch failures.
